subtopic: Data Drift and Concept Drift Detection (KS-Test, PSI)
question_text: [MLOps, Model Serving & Drift Monitoring - Q30] In production MLOps monitoring, what differentiates Concept Drift from Covariate (Data) Drift?

options.text: Covariate drift means P(X) changes while P(Y|X) is constant; Concept drift means the conditional relationship P(Y|X) between features and target labels changes
Concept drift only applies to unsupervised models
Covariate drift requires human ground truth labels to detect
They are synonymous terms in statistical testing

answer_explanation: Covariate drift reflects shifting input distributions P(X) (e.g., younger users sign up), whereas concept drift fundamentally shifts the underlying ground truth mapping P(Y|X) (e.g., fraudster tactics change).
reference_solution: Correct Choice: A. Rationale: Covariate drift reflects shifting input distributions P(X) (e.g., younger users sign up), whereas concept drift fundamentally shifts the underlying ground truth mapping P(Y|X) (e.g., fraudster tactics change).
